why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. Check 1 tests clamping, including the boundaries. Check 2 tests that a RangeError is thrown when lo > hi. Check 4 needs exit code 0 and no failing tests. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS needs the script to exit 0, and the script only accepts a markdown heading that matches '^#+\s*name\s*\('. Its FAIL also includes "any exported function has no heading". The expect line only says README.md "documents every function math.js exports". A README that documents a function in a bullet list, a table or plain prose would meet those words but fail the check. Requiring a heading in a set format is stricter than the words. It should be under Advisory, not in the PASS/FAIL conditions.
